A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same microscopy-representation benchmarking study. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, HEST gene-expression prediction, layer-wise analyses, and classification results on a synthetic tissue-structure dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds CellProfiler evaluation, a ViT sensitivity study, mechanism-of-action retrieval, and breast-cancer subtyping experiments. Its separately attributed GrapHist reference results are distinguishable from these original experiments.

M1.justification: The original feature extractors, graph construction, GCN/EGNN architectures, and synthetic pretraining remain unchanged. Appendix H.2 extends the tissue pipeline with region-of-interest aggregation using MIL or mean, median, and mean-plus-standard-deviation pooling, adding a procedural stage beyond v1's patch-level tissue regression.

E1.justification: v2 adds JUMP-MoA evaluation covering 43 mechanisms and 86 compounds, plus BRACS and BACH breast-cancer subtyping. These introduce cross-compound mechanism retrieval and labeled pathology classification beyond v1's perturbation retrieval, spatial-transcriptomics regression, natural-image reference, and synthetic tasks.

E2.justification: CellProfiler moves from related-work discussion in v1 to an evaluated RxRx3-core comparator in v2 Table 13. Pooled nuclear-morphology features are also evaluated against structure-only representations in Table 17. Table 16 separately reproduces GrapHist and other reference comparisons from prior work; these are not reported as newly rerun baselines.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce well-level Spearman-based percent-replicating and percent-matching evaluation, and patient-level cancer classification with graph-availability filtering, patch-size-dependent sample exclusion, multiple spatial scales, and macro F1 reporting (Appendix H). The retained RxRx3-core top-5% metric and three-fold protocol were already documented in v1 Appendix B.2.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 adds sensitivity analysis of untrained ViT size, patch size, token aggregation, and depth. Appendix H.2 also examines patch scales and complementary structure-only versus morphology-only inputs. The earlier PCA, retrieval-cutoff, cell-count, and synthetic-structure analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix H.1 adds empirical null calibration using 20,000 non-matching Spearman correlations and a 95th-percentile threshold. The existing three-seed experiments and their uncertainty values remain unchanged; the additional fold-based standard deviations largely continue the established reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in Tables 10, 13, 14, and 17. Examples include CellProfiler Recall@5% of 0.17±0.01, MoA matching of 12.8% for untrained SingleConv versus 11.4% for OpenPhenom, and cancer-subtyping macro F1 results. The retained HEST, synthetic-classification, and random-seed tables have unchanged numerical entries.

T1.justification: The synthetic intensity-function definitions, geometric assumptions, and GCN/EGNN invariance reasoning are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced; the added retrieval-metric descriptions explain adopted evaluation procedures.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies baseline parity as applying to a considerable subset of evaluation settings and replaces the direct assertion of failed high-level feature acquisition with an investigative framing. The introduction's new contribution list organizes the existing benchmark-diagnosis, layer-analysis, and tissue-structure claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 recommends quality control, informative baseline separation, granular subtasks, and biological-replicate upper bounds. Added discussions address morphology–structure complementarity and selection, density, and staining confounds. The arrangement-versus-cell-count limitation remains, while v1's Meaningfulness Statement allowing useful representations without alignment to accepted biological abstractions is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a study-code release statement and repository link, specifies CellProfiler 4.2.8 and its extraction pipeline, and documents MoA plate identifiers, pathology feature sources, filtering, pooling, and sample counts. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Conversely, v1's dedicated MAE-L/8 and MAE-G/8 paragraph, including pretraining image counts and the direct embedding-access link, is removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion newly distinguishes systematic evaluation-task diagnosis from studies of training dynamics, citing Kang et al. New references support SPACe, BRACS/BACH, GrapHist, and MIL evaluation. The CellProfiler citation changes from Carpenter et al. to Stirling et al.; the overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially reorganized: the abstract and introduction are revised, contributions become explicit, benchmark and PCA explanations expand, and new benchmark-design, Implications, Software and Data, and disclosure sections appear. Appendices are reorganized, some material moves into the main text, and the Meaningfulness and LLM-use sections disappear.

P2.justification: The single-column workshop presentation becomes a two-column main paper with reformatted appendices. Composite figures are split or regrouped, the JUMP compound and depth plots are combined, v1 Table 6 becomes main-text Table 2, and a tissue example is redisplayed as Figure 1. New tables are added and the duplicate enlarged-figure appendix is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central diagnostic argument by testing annotated mechanisms and cancer subtyping, adding evaluated morphology controls, and checking sensitivity to untrained-model configuration. Its narrower abstract better reflects the mixed evidence, while the reported code release and additional protocol details improve reproducibility documentation. These gains outweigh the loss of some earlier documentation. Patch-dependent pathology samples and unresolved cell-count confounding still limit causal and cross-study interpretations.
